summary.headline: Exicom Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR1.8 crore, while Tritium is being divested at an indicative $85 million EV.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 21.3% YoY to INR277 crore, with the EV charging (EVSE) segment crossing INR100 crore for the first time at INR106 crore (+58.7% YoY). Consolidated revenue grew 37.8% YoY to INR388 crore, but consolidated PAT loss narrowed to INR57.8 crore, and consolidated EBITDA swung to +INR1.8 crore from a loss of INR32.7 crore a year earlier. The Board approved divesting 100% of the Tritium Group after receiving a non-binding term sheet at an indicative $85 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis, with closure targeted for December 2026. Management said the order book of about INR1,645 crore gives around 15 months of revenue visibility, and guidance for FY28 will come with Q4 results.

segments.name: EV Charging (EVSE, standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue of INR106 crore in Q2, first time above INR100 crore; H1 standalone EV revenue INR167 crore vs INR120 crore. Management says volumes are about 90% higher than Q2 FY26, and export mix is around 5% currently.

segments.name: Critical Power (telecom, standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue of INR171 crore in Q2, up 5.8% YoY. Management points to BharatNet Phase 3 revenue visibility of INR235 crore in FY27 and INR478 crore in FY28.

segments.name: Tritium (EV charging subsidiary, consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose about 133% per management, and it contributed about 27% of consolidated revenue in H1 FY27. Order intake was INR14.7 million in Q2 vs INR17 million in Q1, with a backlog of about INR23 million; consolidated losses continue during the ramp-up phase.

segments.name: Battery energy storage (BESS)
segments.commentary: Focused on commercial, industrial and SOHO segments. About 35 small projects (about 10 MWh) executed; order book about 30 MWh. Management sees pilot revenue this year and about INR150 crore of revenue next year.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance to be released with Q4 FY27 results; management said there will be growth in both segments next year, but did not quantify it.
Order book and advanced pipeline of about INR1,645-1,650 crore gives revenue visibility of about INR1,600 crore over the next 15 months.

Tritium divestment: non-binding term sheet for 100% sale at an indicative $85 million, cash-free debt-free; target closing December 2026, may slip into next quarter. Management expects a net cash position if closed.
Tritium expected to reach EBITDA breakeven sometime in FY28, per management.
Exports targeted at 30% of revenue over the next three years; FY28 expected to be the first fully scaled export year, with at least 3x growth in export revenue vs FY27.
Management expects some write-down on Exicom's investment in Tritium, which it says will be partly offset by power module supply and EV technology sales to Tritium.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad manufacturing facility fully operational; Gurgaon-to-Hyderabad transition substantially complete, with fixed cost intensity falling as volumes ramp.
Over INR200 crore of capex deployed in March 2026; full-quarter depreciation of the Hyderabad plant (INR10.8 crore in Q2) is weighing on PAT.
A liquid-cooled power module line has been set up in Hyderabad to manufacture modules for Tritium.
DC-FLEX and GRID-FLEX products enter mass production in April and July 2027 respectively, under rate contracts with large customers for 3 to 5 years (KTM segment).
demand_pricing: Industry EV sales growing at about 50% CAGR; India's H1 FY27 EV sales already exceed all of FY26. Management expects about 12 lakh AC chargers and 25,000 DC chargers to be needed by FY30.
Exicom works with 7 of the top 10 passenger vehicle OEMs and 17 of the top 20 charge point operators.
Telecom: 5G subscribers rose from about 25 crore to about 45 crore; management sees 60,000-80,000 power conversion systems per year and about 8 lakh lithium-ion batteries of demand over three years.
Competition in bus and truck charging is tender-based with cost as the main criterion; management says its market share there is lower than with passenger car OEMs.
Management said commodity, semiconductor and forex cost increases compressed unit-level contribution margins in Q2, partly offset by operating leverage. Pass-through to customers has not been easy.
Government-backed BharatNet tenders have fixed prices, so price revisions are not generally possible; the company says it is on track for the expected second-half site deliveries.

qa_highlights.question: Srinivasan Reddy asked how much cash will reach Exicom from the Tritium sale after debt, leases and minority interest, and whether the subsidiary investment will be written down.
qa_highlights.answer: Management is still working through customary adjustments and will update the final amount later. It expects some write-down, which it says will be partly offset by power module supply to Tritium and EV technology monetisation.

qa_highlights.question: Srinivasan Reddy asked whether the retained TRI-FLEX licence and Gen 2 power module manufacturing agreement are exclusive, their term, and whether minimum volumes are committed.
qa_highlights.answer: These terms are still under negotiation. Management expects substantial revenue from module supply, but said exclusivity is unlikely because customers diversify suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Srinivasan Reddy asked whether BharatNet deliveries (about 5,400 sites in H1 vs about 12,600 in H2) are on track and whether higher sales and forex costs can be passed on.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is broadly on track, with figures treated as directional. Because the orders are backed by government tenders, price revisions are usually not possible.

qa_highlights.question: Mithun Maity asked why Tritium is being sold when it was expected to reach positive EBITDA in Q3 and Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the need for large investment in power infrastructure for data centres and heavy working capital needs. It also said home-market and export growth need capital, so the sale was a judgement on the best use of capital.

qa_highlights.question: Mithun Maity asked for domestic standalone guidance for FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance will be given before the end of FY27 with Q4 results. The INR1,600 crore order book is a 15-month visibility figure, not a FY28 revenue forecast.

qa_highlights.question: Mithun Maity asked how the company differentiates from new EV charger entrants.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the widest EV charger product range in India, the highest R&D spend in the country, long OEM approval cycles and capacity, and a service network in more than 200 towns and cities.

qa_highlights.question: Kushal asked about EVSE versus telecom margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose segment margins. It said unit-level margins were compressed this quarter by commodity and semiconductor costs, but group EBITDA margin improved due to operating leverage.

risks_watch: Tritium sale: final cash proceeds and any write-down are unquantified; the non-binding term sheet still needs a definitive agreement, and closing may slip past December 2026.
Commodity, semiconductor and forex cost inflation may keep compressing unit margins if price pass-through is limited.
Execution risk on BharatNet Phase 3 (INR235 crore FY27 and INR478 crore FY28 visibility, with possible slippage into FY29) and the tender-priced bus and truck segments.
Competition in EV charging from new entrants; management acknowledged some customers were lost.
Depreciation from the Hyderabad plant and Tritium amortisation keep PAT negative despite positive EBITDA.
Export targets (30% of revenue in three years) depend on new markets, with exports currently at about 5-10% of mix.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on standalone EV and telecom growth and the operating leverage turnaround. Cautious and somewhat evasive on Tritium economics, the sale proceeds and write-down, and on FY28 guidance, which is deferred to Q4.

key_quotes: This quarter the company delivered a turnaround result, both in terms of stand-alone and consolidated performance.
The 3 defining milestones this quarter was, one, EVSE business delivered its highest ever quarter, crossing INR100 crores mark on a stand-alone basis for the first time in the history of the company.
So we had to make a judicious call to see which is the best use of capital in terms of investment, to get best returns for the shareholders for a certain amount of risk.
But the exact guidance we'll be able to give you in quarter 4 results.
So we disclose it only on the company level, but owing to, as the question was asked before, there is always a phase when the competition is intense.

adds.what: Hyderabad manufacturing facility (fully operational; Gurgaon-to-Hyderabad transition substantially complete)
Liquid-cooled power module line in Hyderabad for Tritium modules
DC-FLEX product mass production (KTM segment, rate contracts)
GRID-FLEX product mass production (KTM segment, rate contracts)

growth.why: Management gives no quantified FY28 growth (only 'growth in both segments', to be released with Q4 FY27), but backs it with an INR1,645 crore order book (~15 months visibility), BESS revenue of ~INR150 crore next year, BharatNet Phase 3 visibility of INR478 crore in FY28, and exports to triple in FY27; consolidated revenue grew 37.8% YoY and consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR1.8 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin rose to 9.2% in Q2 from 6.6% a year ago and INR20.9 crore in Q1, and consolidated EBITDA turned to +INR1.8 crore from -INR32.7 crore, driven by operating leverage, though unit margins were compressed by commodity and forex costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hyderabad plant is fully operational and a liquid-cooled module line is set up, with DC-FLEX mass production in April 2027 and GRID-FLEX in July 2027 under 3-5 year rate contracts, though no new plant beyond these is quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone EVSE revenue hit INR106 crore (+58.7% YoY) with volumes about 90% higher YoY, an INR1,645 crore order book gives about 15 months of visibility, and BharatNet Phase 3 visibility is INR235 crore in FY27 and INR478 crore in FY28.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY28 guidance is deferred to Q4 FY27 with growth in both segments left unquantified, and management has not given a numerical upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Tritium sale carries an unquantified write-down, closing may slip past December 2026, and commodity and forex inflation may keep compressing unit margins if pass-through stays limited.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: DC-FLEX enters mass production in April 2027 and GRID-FLEX in July 2027, and BESS is targeted at about INR150 crore of revenue next year, with pilot revenue this year.

rows.label: Tritium divestment at indicative $85M EV
rows.why: Non-binding term sheet for 100% sale, cash-free debt-free, with management expecting a net cash position on closing, though proceeds and write-down are unquantified and closing may slip a quarter.

rows.label: Export revenue to triple in FY27 and reach 30% of sales in 3 years
rows.why: Exports are currently about 5% of mix (5-10% per risks), so the 3x FY27 target and 30% share in three years depend on new markets not yet proven.

rows.label: INR1,645 crore order book and advanced pipeline
rows.why: Order book gives about 15 months of revenue visibility, with about INR1,600 crore expected over that period, supporting consolidated revenue that grew 37.8% YoY to INR388 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on standalone EV and telecom growth, operating leverage and the order book, but cautious and somewhat evasive on Tritium proceeds, write-down and FY28 guidance; analysts pressed on why Tritium is being sold when it was near positive EBITDA and on FY28 domestic guidance.

oneOffs.what: Expected write-down on Tritium investment, not yet quantified; would hit profit, not revenue growth

quality.why: Consolidated revenue grew 37.8% YoY to INR388 crore, mainly from EVSE (+91.3% to INR214 crore) with management citing standalone EV volumes about 90% higher YoY, while Critical Power was flat at INR175 crore; no one-off revenue item is disclosed, and the pending Tritium write-down is unquantified and affects profit rather than growth.
